title: Dark Web Safety & Lawful Onion Resources
boundary: This guide supports lawful privacy, censorship resistance, journalism, whistleblowing, defensive research and access to verified public-interest onion services. It does not provide links, mirrors, invitations, vendor information or operational guidance for illicit markets, stolen data, malware services, weapons, drugs, exploitation material or other criminal activity.

definitions.meaning: Public pages reachable through ordinary browsers and commonly indexed by search engines.
Content not indexed publicly, such as private email, banking, medical portals and authenticated databases. Most of the deep web is ordinary and lawful.
Services intentionally reachable through anonymity networks such as Tor. A Tor onion service uses a 56-character v3 address ending in .onion.
A hardened browser that routes traffic through the Tor network and reduces tracking and fingerprinting when used with its defaults.
A service reachable only through Tor. Traffic remains inside Tor and is end-to-end encrypted between Tor Browser and the onion service.

steps.title: Define the lawful purpose and threat model
steps.body: Write down why Tor is needed, what identity or information must be protected, who could observe the activity, how long separation must last and what consequences a failure would have. Ordinary privacy, whistleblowing and high-risk targeted research require different systems.

steps.title: Choose the correct environment
steps.body: Use Tor Browser on a fully updated everyday computer for low-risk private reading. Use Tails from a verified USB for an amnesic session. Use Qubes OS with Whonix for persistent high-risk compartmentation. Do not assume a virtual machine automatically hides activity from a compromised host.

steps.title: Download only from the official project
steps.body: Obtain Tor Browser from torproject.org or Tails from tails.net. Verify the download signature or verification result before installation. Never install a repackaged browser from a forum, file host, torrent, advertisement or onion directory.

steps.title: Separate the research identity
steps.body: Do not log into personal email, social media, cloud storage or accounts previously used outside Tor. Do not reuse usernames, profile images, phone numbers, writing signatures, recovery addresses or schedules. Identity separation is more important than adding another network layer.

steps.title: Connect safely
steps.body: Connect Tor Browser directly in most ordinary environments. Use official Tor bridges or Snowflake only where Tor is blocked or where revealing Tor use creates risk. A VPN is not required for Tor and merely moves trust to another provider; no free VPN is recommended.

steps.title: Set the security level before browsing
steps.body: For unknown onion services, use Tor Browser's Safer or Safest security level. Safest disables more active web features but can break sites. Do not add extensions, change about:config settings, resize the window unusually or install plugins because customisation can make the browser fingerprint more unique.

steps.title: Obtain onion addresses from an authoritative clearnet source
steps.body: Prefer a service's official clearnet page, SecureDrop Directory or Tor Browser's Onion-Location prompt. Confirm the full 56-character v3 address. Never trust a Hidden Wiki, random paste, social-media reply, search advertisement, URL shortener or unsolicited message.

steps.title: Verify the address before every sensitive visit
steps.body: Compare the entire onion address with the official source, not only the first few memorable characters. Bookmark the verified address inside the isolated profile. Phishing clones can copy branding, login forms and PGP text while using a different onion key.

steps.title: Browse without creating identifying links
steps.body: Do not enter personal details, reuse passwords, make payments, connect wallets, upload identity documents or allow notification prompts. Do not use Tor for ordinary personal accounts in the same compartment used for anonymous research.

steps.title: Treat every download as hostile
steps.body: Avoid downloading files. When a lawful public-interest document is necessary, record the source and hash, keep the original unopened, convert a copy through Dangerzone or open it in a disposable offline compartment. Never enable macros, scripts, external content or embedded media.

steps.title: Use purpose-built submission and transfer tools
steps.body: Use the official SecureDrop Directory to locate news organisations and OnionShare for controlled Tor-based file transfer. Read the recipient's instructions first. Remove metadata with MAT2 or ExifTool when appropriate, but preserve an untouched original separately when evidential integrity matters.

steps.title: End the session deliberately
steps.body: Close Tor Browser and shut down Tails rather than leaving the environment suspended. Remove temporary notes, disconnect removable media and keep any lawful evidence in an encrypted, documented archive outside the browsing compartment. Review what personal or behavioural information may have been revealed.

tools.name: Tor Browser
tools.purpose: Default browser for lawful onion services and private web access.
tools.bestFor: Low-to-moderate risk reading and censorship resistance.
tools.limit: Cannot protect an infected device, unsafe login, identifying behaviour or files opened outside Tor.

tools.name: Tails
tools.purpose: Amnesic operating system routing internet activity through Tor.
tools.bestFor: Temporary high-separation sessions from a verified USB.
tools.limit: Not magic; firmware, hardware, behaviour, persistent storage and unsafe files can still expose a user.

tools.name: Qubes OS
tools.purpose: Compartmentalises tasks into isolated virtual machines.
tools.bestFor: Persistent advanced research with separate identities and disposable file handling.
tools.limit: Requires compatible hardware and disciplined use; it is not anonymous without an anonymity compartment.

tools.name: Whonix
tools.purpose: Separates Tor routing into a gateway and workstation.
tools.bestFor: Persistent Tor applications, especially inside Qubes OS.
tools.limit: Host compromise, identity reuse and simultaneous Tor/non-Tor activity can defeat separation.

tools.name: OnionShare
tools.purpose: Tor-based file transfer, receive mode, temporary site hosting and chat.
tools.bestFor: Controlled direct transfer without conventional cloud hosting.
tools.limit: Protect the generated address; a recipient can copy or redistribute anything received.

tools.name: Dangerzone
tools.purpose: Converts potentially malicious documents into safer PDFs inside isolated containers.
tools.bestFor: Reading lawful documents received from unknown or sensitive sources.
tools.limit: Conversion may change formatting and cannot make an already compromised host safe.

tools.name: MAT2
tools.bestFor: Preparing copies for lawful publication or transfer.
tools.limit: Metadata removal does not remove visible clues, cloud logs, file hashes or all proprietary data.

tools.name: KeePassXC
tools.purpose: Local encrypted credentials and unique research-identity passwords.
tools.bestFor: Keeping compartment-specific credentials offline from hosted password services.
tools.limit: The user must protect and back up the encrypted database without mixing identity compartments.

officialOnions.name: DuckDuckGo Onion Service
officialOnions.purpose: A basic onion-service connection test and privacy-oriented search interface.
officialOnions.verification: Published by the Tor Project in its onion-service troubleshooting documentation.
officialOnions.warning: Search results are not endorsements. Do not use results to discover illicit markets or trust unknown onion addresses.

officialOnions.name: SecureDrop Directory
officialOnions.purpose: Official directory of active SecureDrop instances operated by news and public-interest organisations.
officialOnions.verification: The onion address is published in the footer of the official SecureDrop Directory.
officialOnions.warning: Choose the organisation deliberately and follow its source instructions. SecureDrop protects a channel, not careless identity disclosure.

officialOnions.name: OnionShare Official Site
officialOnions.purpose: Official OnionShare project site and download information over Tor.
officialOnions.verification: The project publishes the address and proof on its official clearnet website.
officialOnions.warning: Download software only after verifying the official source and published signatures.

officialOnions.name: CIA Official Onion Site
officialOnions.purpose: Official CIA public site and reporting-information route over Tor.
officialOnions.verification: The exact address is published by the CIA on its official website.
officialOnions.warning: Contacting any government organisation has serious consequences. Read the official reporting instructions and obtain independent legal advice where appropriate.

dangerCategories.title: Hidden Wiki and random onion directories
reasons: Phishing clones can replace legitimate addresses with attacker-controlled lookalikes.
Directories frequently mix lawful resources with scams, malware and illegal content.
Operators and mirrors can change without notice and may be compromised.
dangerCategories.rule: Do not use general onion directories. Obtain addresses from the organisation's official clearnet page or a recognised project directory.

dangerCategories.title: Illicit drug, weapon and counterfeit markets
reasons: Participation can be criminal and transactions create financial, postal and device evidence.
Markets are frequently exit scams, law-enforcement operations or compromised services.
Listings can contain fentanyl, fraud, malware, coercion and false escrow claims.
dangerCategories.rule: Do not visit, register, transact, contact vendors or seek mirrors. This page intentionally publishes no market addresses.

dangerCategories.title: Stolen credentials, carding and identity-data shops
reasons: Possession or use of stolen data can cause direct harm and criminal liability.
Downloads commonly contain malware, fake datasets or material designed to identify buyers.
Payment and account activity can link a user to a criminal service.
dangerCategories.rule: Use breach-notification services only to protect accounts you own. Never acquire or test third-party credentials.

dangerCategories.title: Malware, exploit and cybercrime-as-a-service forums
reasons: Tools and samples may infect the visitor rather than the stated target.
Forums can be monitored, seized or operated by law enforcement.
Requests for services, targets or access can create evidence of intent.
dangerCategories.rule: Use legal training labs, CTFs and defensive repositories. Do not access criminal service forums or download unknown samples.

dangerCategories.title: Unknown leak dumps and file archives
reasons: Archives can contain malware, personal data, exploitation material or illegal content.
Opening files may reveal the real IP address, device information or document-reader vulnerabilities.
Downloading or redistributing data can harm victims and destroy evidential context.
dangerCategories.rule: Use established public-interest publishers and verified evidence archives. Never download random dumps.

dangerCategories.title: Fake hitman, hacking and recovery services
reasons: Many are extortion scams designed to collect payment and identifying information.
Contact can create legal risk even when the claimed service is fake.
Operators may threaten to expose messages or demand further payment.
dangerCategories.rule: Do not contact or test these services. Threats or extortion should be documented safely and reported to appropriate authorities.

dangerCategories.title: Crypto investment, mixing and escrow offers
reasons: Fake escrow and investment schemes frequently steal deposits.
Transactions are permanently observable and can trigger sanctions, anti-money-laundering or criminal investigations.
Wallet software and QR codes may redirect funds or install malware.
dangerCategories.rule: Do not connect wallets, sign transactions or send funds to unknown onion services.

dangerCategories.title: Ransomware leak sites
reasons: They distribute stolen victim data and may host weaponised downloads.
Visiting or downloading can expose victims further and create legal or ethical problems.
Sites may fingerprint visitors or redirect to malicious infrastructure.
dangerCategories.rule: Use trusted cybersecurity reporting and official incident notices instead of visiting leak portals.

dangerCategories.title: Illegal exploitation material
reasons: Possession, viewing, saving or sharing may be criminal and causes direct harm to victims.
Services can be scams, malware traps or law-enforcement operations.
Accidental exposure can be psychologically traumatic.
dangerCategories.rule: Close the page immediately. Do not save, screenshot, forward or investigate the content. Report through an official national channel such as the IWF or NCMEC CyberTipline where applicable.

enforcementCases.name: Archetyp Market
enforcementCases.lesson: A long-running market with a large user base was taken offline through coordinated action across multiple countries. Longevity and reputation did not create safety.

enforcementCases.name: Nemesis Market
enforcementCases.category: Drugs, stolen data and cybercrime services
enforcementCases.lesson: Authorities reported seizing servers and cryptocurrency and retaining platform data for investigations of sellers and users.

enforcementCases.name: Hydra Market
enforcementCases.category: Russian-language illicit marketplace and financial services
enforcementCases.lesson: A large established ecosystem can be disrupted through infrastructure seizure, cryptocurrency analysis and international cooperation.

enforcementCases.name: DarkMarket
enforcementCases.lesson: Infrastructure investigations can expose administrators and produce evidence for follow-on cases against vendors and users.

enforcementCases.name: AlphaBay and Hansa
enforcementCases.lesson: Hansa was covertly controlled by law enforcement while users migrated to it after AlphaBay disappeared. A functioning site can be an active evidence-collection environment.

enforcementCases.name: Silk Road
enforcementCases.lesson: Pseudonyms, Tor and cryptocurrency did not prevent identification through operational mistakes, financial evidence and conventional investigation.

emergency.scenario: You clicked an unknown onion link
emergency.action: Do not interact, download, log in or grant permissions. Close the tab. If Tor Browser behaved unexpectedly, close the browser and restart the isolated session.
Do not open it. Disconnect the research environment, record the filename and hash if lawful to retain, and delete or quarantine it using an authorised defensive workflow.
From a known-clean non-Tor device, change that password anywhere it was reused, enable MFA and review active sessions. Do not revisit the onion site.
Stop further contact and preserve transaction records. Do not pay recovery services or extortion demands. Seek legal and law-enforcement guidance appropriate to the jurisdiction.
Close it immediately. Do not save or redistribute it. Report the URL through an official national reporting channel. In the UK use the Internet Watch Foundation; in the US use NCMEC CyberTipline.
Disconnect the device from networks, avoid logging into important accounts, preserve volatile evidence only if trained, and seek qualified incident-response help from a separate clean device.
